transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I came in because... I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and a disappointment. I had this one near-miss at work, and it just... it feels like it proves I'm not meant to be a nurse. I just keep thinking lately that everyone would be better off without me.
Have you ever felt this way for a period of two weeks or longer at any point in your life before this current experience?

Actually, it's... well, it's not really a separate time before this. This whole feeling has just been going on for about a year and two months now. It all started right after I graduated high school and began my college classes and taking on full-time clinic work.
Over the past year, have you been experiencing a significant loss of interest or pleasure in almost all of the activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to do things to clear my head, like... jogging, knitting, cooking, or just reading a book after class. But now... I just come home and sit on my bed in my scrubs. I just can't make myself care about any of those things anymore.
During this past year, have you experienced any periods where your symptoms were so severe that you were unable to function at work or take care of your basic personal needs for at least two weeks?

Yeah, it definitely has. Um, I’ve fallen pretty far behind in my nursing prerequisites for school. And at work... I've had to start asking my coworkers to double-check tasks that I used to handle confidently on my own. It just makes me really afraid to take on my normal clinic responsibilities right now.
